clue.text: Maiden I run after gets wrong impression

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
to sprint is to run fast

explanation.surface: A young woman runs off after someone and is badly misjudged.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket scoring M stands for a maiden (an over with no runs); the pieces simply follow one another.
explanation.definitionFit: A misprint is a typographical error, literally a faulty impression made by the press.

clue.text: An unusual diet, can one suggest?

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: unusual tells us the letters of these words are put into a strange new order

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether an odd eating plan might be put forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges DIET and CAN to give NDICATE; I (one) comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: To indicate something is to point it out or hint at it, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Expectation of new clock in gift wrapping

indicators.note: wrapping says the gift word is placed all round the other pieces

parts.note: a present is a gift
to clock a runner is to time them

explanation.surface: Someone anticipates a new clock arriving as a wrapped present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clock' looks like a noun but is a verb: to clock a runner is to time them.
explanation.definitionFit: A presentiment is a feeling that something is about to happen, a foreboding or anticipation.

clue.text: Living on square in 'bad surroundings

indicators.note: bad surroundings means the word for bad goes round the other piece

parts.note: immoral means bad, wicked
a T-square gives T as a short form for square

explanation.surface: Someone lives on a town square amid a rough neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Living on' looks like part of the scene but defines the answer: something that lives on for ever. T goes inside IMMORAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something deathless continues existing for ever, so it keeps going without end.

clue.text: Supporter of Napoleon, say.

parts.note: Napoleon is the pig leader in Orwell's Animal Farm, and a pig's foot holds it up

explanation.surface: A loyal follower of the French emperor is described.
explanation.walkthrough: The French emperor is a false trail: think of Orwell's pig Napoleon in Animal Farm, whose feet support him.
explanation.definitionFit: A pig's foot, cooked as food, is the thing that bears the pig's weight.

clue.text: A fellow concealing money in niche

indicators.note: concealing says the fellow word hides another piece within it

parts.note: cove is old British slang for a man or fellow
L is the symbol for a pound, a unit of money

explanation.surface: A man hides his cash in a recess in the wall.
explanation.walkthrough: COVE is dated British slang for a chap; L (pound sterling) goes inside A COVE.
explanation.definitionFit: An alcove is a recess set back in a wall, much like a niche.

clue.text: A saintly band?

parts.note: not a group of holy people but the bright ring drawn round a saint's head

explanation.surface: A group of holy people forms a band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' suggests a group of musicians or people, but it means a ring of light.
explanation.definitionFit: Saints are painted with a circle of light above or around the head.

clue.text: People generally curse such clothing

parts.note: men, in old usage, means people in general, mankind
to swear is to curse

explanation.surface: Folk swear at certain garments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'such' points back to men: the clothing is clothing for men.
explanation.definitionFit: Garments made for male customers form the department of that name in a shop.

clue.text: Set down, for example, in detail

indicators.note: in puts the example abbreviation inside the word for detail

parts.note: to detail events is to relate them
EG is the abbreviation of exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: An instruction to write something down with an example, in full detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detail' looks like a noun but is a verb here, meaning to recount events.
explanation.definitionFit: To relegate a team is to demote it, moving it down a division.

clue.text: Advantage held by trained geologist

indicators.note: held by means the letters are contained within the following words

explanation.surface: A trained earth scientist holds the upper hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the edge over a rival means having a slight lead over them.

clue.text: Meagre food: and little drink served by the lower classes

parts.note: a short is a small measure of spirits
the commons are the common people, below the nobility

explanation.surface: Poor rations and small glasses are handed out to the working class.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'short' is British for a small measure of spirits such as whisky; 'served by' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on short commons is an idiom for having scant rations, a meagre allowance of food.

clue.text: Attractive tunnel may be a danger to shipping

parts.note: magnetic means attractive, drawing things to it
a mine is a tunnel dug underground

explanation.surface: An appealing underground passage might threaten ships.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attractive' looks like praise, but it means drawing iron, as a magnet does.
explanation.definitionFit: This naval weapon explodes when a steel hull passes near, sinking vessels.

clue.text: Vehicle with clear licence

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
to clear a sum is to make it as net profit

explanation.surface: A car comes with an unambiguous permit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clear' means to earn after deductions, as in clearing a profit, so NET.
explanation.definitionFit: A carnet is a customs permit allowing a vehicle or goods across borders.

clue.text: Power switch — for Greens, that, is

indicators.note: switch means the letters are swapped around into a new order

parts.note: ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A call for the Green party to switch to some new power source.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switch' rearranges GREENS together with IE (that is).
explanation.definitionFit: To energise a circuit is to supply it with electrical current, to drive it.

clue.text: Clearly a painter to secure large return

indicators.note: to secure means the painter's name holds the reversed piece inside it

parts.note: Sir Peter Lely was a portrait painter at the court of Charles II

indicators.note: return means the word for large is turned back to front

parts.note: big means large

explanation.surface: An artist plainly wants a big payback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns the word for large backwards to give GIB. Lely was a Dutch-born portrait painter at the Stuart court.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing done legibly can be read plainly and without difficulty.

clue.text: He sounds like a Yorkist

indicators.note: sounds like signals a word said aloud matching another spelling

parts.note: here a Yorkshireman, a man from Leeds

explanation.surface: Someone talks with a York accent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sounds' is the definition: the sailor who takes depth soundings with a lead line. 'like' signals the homophone of LEEDS MAN, a Yorkshireman.
explanation.definitionFit: The seaman who heaves the lead to measure water depth takes soundings.

clue.text: Pilot keeps record with a nearer-vertical climb

indicators.note: keeps means the steering word holds the record word within it

parts.note: to pilot a vessel is to steer it
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: An aviator holds on to the logbook during a sharp ascent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pilot' looks like a noun but is a verb; an EP is an extended-play vinyl record.
explanation.definitionFit: A slope rising more sharply than another is the more precipitous of the two.

clue.text: Footwork or holding — nothing to distinguish ring fighter

indicators.note: holding says the footwork word grips the zero inside it

parts.note: tread, a step, is footwork
O is the round shape of zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A boxing coach debates footwork against holding.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a boxing ring, with its footwork and holding, but the ring is a bullring.
explanation.definitionFit: A bullfighter fights in the bullring, so is a fighter in a ring.

clue.text: Roundly condemn river transport of inferior quality

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon
a crate is slang for a decrepit old car or plane

explanation.surface: A complaint about poor-quality boats on a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The EXE is a river in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: To execrate someone is to denounce or curse them bitterly.

clue.text: Soldiers receive his order before start of gunfire in engagement

indicators.note: receive means the soldiers word takes another piece inside it

parts.note: men are ordinary soldiers

indicators.note: order tells us the letters of the word his are rearranged
start of means take only the opening letter of gunfire

explanation.surface: Troops get his command before shooting begins in battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engagement' suggests a battle, but means gear teeth engaging. 'order' rearranges HIS to SHI.
explanation.definitionFit: Gear teeth that mesh are interlocked with each other, working together.

clue.text: One missing an insect — it gets dispatched inside

parts.note: an gives the letter A

indicators.note: inside says the dispatched word goes within the insect word

parts.note: a bee is an insect
sent means dispatched

explanation.surface: A bee goes missing after being sent off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it gets dispatched inside' says the word for dispatched sits within the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is not present where expected is away, missing from the roll.

clue.text: Failing: to catch up in sport

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a sin is a moral failing
to net a fish is to catch it

explanation.surface: A player falls short in trying to catch up in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses SIN + NET, the pieces read backwards together.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a racket game played over a net, an example of a sport.

clue.text: Elevated or cast down, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that a word is said aloud to match another

parts.note: razed means demolished, cast down to the ground

explanation.surface: Someone is either lifted up or thrown down.
explanation.walkthrough: RAZED (torn down) and the answer sound alike but mean opposites.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lifted up has been set higher, a plain synonym.

clue.text: More than this, concoction required for stimulus?

indicators.note: a concoction is a mixture, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A drinker wonders whether a stronger brew is needed for a lift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concoction' rearranges the letters of MORE THAN THIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A boost or fillip is figuratively an injection that revives something.

clue.text: Topless witches in a hot place

indicators.note: topless in a down clue means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a coven is a gathering of witches

explanation.surface: Bare-breasted witches gather somewhere warm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topless' removes the first letter C from COVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen oven is an enclosed space heated for cooking.

clue.text: Rain storm in the country

indicators.note: storm suggests turbulence, so the letters of rain are tossed about

explanation.surface: Bad weather hits the rural countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the country' suggests rural land, but it is a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Iran is a nation in the Middle East.

clue.text: Disinclination to maintain offspring without investments initially

parts.note: to aver is to maintain or assert

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the offspring word goes around the next piece

parts.note: a son is offspring

indicators.note: initially means take only the first letter of investments

explanation.surface: Reluctance to support a child when there is no money invested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside, not lacking: SON goes round I (investments initially).
explanation.definitionFit: An aversion is a strong dislike, an unwillingness towards something.

clue.text: Frightful danger to monarch from one responsible for plots

indicators.note: frightful suggests something in a terrible state, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A dreadful threat to the sovereign comes from a plotter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plots' suggests conspiracy, but means garden beds. ER is Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who tends flower beds and vegetable patches looks after garden plots.
